## Historical audit: S0099

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/external_followup/fixed_h0/selected/external_followup/bw_0011/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines. All supplied observations are whole lines; none is split.

| Evidence | Observation and qualification |
|---|---|
| Line 1, student request | **Goal:** reconstruct a reference clean laboratory for a progress report: blue paneled corner, coved floor, suspended grid and exposed services, glass-fronted cabinet, dandelion mural and clock. The requested camera and materials should match the image. The adapted runner, not the program, controls saving and rendering. This is the requested scene, not independently observed image content. |
| Lines 3–5, student response, execute 1, result | The first program specified separate walls, cabinet parts and shelves, mural fibers, ceiling components, display, materials, camera and lights. Execution failed at the cabinet glass: the .085 fillet exceeded half its .018 thickness. No image was returned. Later code in that program was not reached. |
| Lines 6, 8–10, feedback, student revision, execute 2, result | The student received the traceback, reduced the pane fillet to .008 and replaced the solid cabinet body with separate back, sides and caps. The second execution timed out after about 600 seconds with empty logs and no image. Whether the fillet fix completed successfully is not established. |
| Lines 11, 13–15, feedback, student revision, execute 3, result | After receiving the timeout, the student replaced many individual solid mural tubes with shared planar ribbon meshes and lowered requested Cycles samples. Execution failed at mural material assignment because `ob.data` was `None`; no image was returned. The timeout’s cause is unknown, so the optimization is a hypothesis, not a validated diagnosis. |
| Lines 16–18, feedback and student response | With zero executions remaining, the student supplied another complete program, guarding material assignment by mesh type and non-null data. This is an **unexecuted revision**, not a demonstrated fix or successful submission. |

**Scene checks.** The programs specify multiple objects and differentiated metal, glass, procedural mural and concrete finishes. Cabinet parts are grouped and positioned together; coves and ceiling supports are specified, but physical connections, intersections and visibility are unverified. The scene is architectural rather than articulated, so no human or object pose is established. A fixed corner camera, LED-associated emitters, additional area lights and world illumination are specified; the additional illumination differs from the request for LED-only lighting. No returned render permits evaluation of framing, lighting uniformity, texture appearance, occlusion or reference fidelity (lines 9–10, 14–15).

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input or teacher detection, diagnosis, proposal, execution or adoption is visible. The student autonomously revised programs in response to runner errors; sessions report no student tool calls (lines 2, 7, 12, 17). Runner feedback is not teacher advice.

**Outcome and lessons.** Observed outcome is **algorithmic build failures plus a technical timeout**, with no successful build or render shown—not an empty patch or formal success. Transferably, dimensional constraints and object-data types matter, and an untested correction remains uncertain. The fillet dimensions and particular mural implementation are task-specific. Whether ribbon consolidation would resolve the timeout, and whether the final program would run or match the image, remain unresolved.
